question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to the integral ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=\sqrt{y}\,i+{e}^{x}\,j$ and $C$ is the curve $\operatorname{ln}⁡y=x-2$ traversed from the point $A(2,1)$ to the point $B(4,{e}^{2})?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+2)\,i+t\,j.$*

current_example.problem: Evaluate $\displaystyle \int\limits_{C} \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r},$ where $\mathbf F(x, y) = y\,\mathbf{i} + x\,\mathbf{j}$ and $C$ is the curve $y^3 = x-5$ traversed from the point $A(5,0)$ to the point $B(6,1).$
current_example.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
y^3 = x-5
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
x = y^3 + 5.
$$

So, we can parametrize the curve using

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}+5)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = t^3+5, \qquad
y = t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,j \\  & =t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+5)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =t\cdot 3{t}^{2}+({t}^{3}+5)\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{3}+{t}^{3}+5 \\  & =4{t}^{3}+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{3}+5\,dt \\  & ={[{t}^{4}+5t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1+5-0 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
